Judges

Introduction

The document of Judges, these are gathered stories of Israil from their attacking of Kanaan up_to the time that the ones_ruling Israil were kings. It's told in this reading the big acts of their warriors that called “Judges.” Most of them were leaders of soldiers, and not judges according to our(incl) understanding of this word. Samsun is most recognized of them all. What he did will_be_read there at chapters 13–16.

This is what we(incl) can learn on this reading: Israil succeeded because they followed_submissively of the command of God (MS Manama), but their distancing from him what caused_destruction of them. God is always ready to save his people at the time that they turn_back on their sins, and they will_return again there to him.

And due to that, the Israilitas hid there in the mountains and there in the caves, and there in the places that could_be_hiding_place. 3 And when the Israilitas plant, the (ones) from_Midiyan, (ones) from_Amalik, and the residents of the east attacked them. 4 They camp there in Israil and destroy the plants of the Israilitas until Gasa. 19 Therefore, Gidyun went_ his _home quickly. He cooked a young goat, and he cooked a bread with no leaven from the flour put on a winnowing_tray. And he brought all that he cooked there to the angel who was there near the uk tree. 20 And the angel of God said to him, “Put_ the viand and the bread without leaven _on this stone and pour it with soup.” And Gidyun did it. 21 And the angel of the Lord God touched with his staff the viand and the bread. 25 On that evening, the Lord God told Gidyun, “Get(sg) the second bull of cow of your(sg) father, the cow that's seven years_old. And destroy(sg) the altar for Baal of your(sg) father, and put_down(sg) the post false_god Asira which was there beside the altar. 26 Afterwards, make(sg) a good altar here on this mountain for me the Lord God of yours(sg), put_ the stones of the altar _over_each_other properly. 28 When the residents of the town woke up at dawn, they saw that the altar of Baal was torn_down and the post false_god Asira fell already. We(excl) will_kill him because he torn_down the altar of Baal and put_down our(incl) god which is the pole Asira.”

We(incl) will_do it like this again, dry_up(sg) the wool and occupy(sg) the surrounding ground with dew.” 40 And God did it in the evening. The defeating of Gidyun with the (ones) from_Midiyan

71 Hirub-Baal (that is Gidyun) and his soldiers woke_up early. And they camped there beside the spring of Harud. And the camp of the (ones) from_Midiyas was there at the valley on their north (LIT left_side), that's near mountain of Muri.

They might boast that they defeated the (ones) from_Midiyan because of their strength and not because of me. 3 [xr]So then, tell(sg) the people, ‘Who are those afraid and tremble with fear, leave(pl) here in the mountain and go_home(pl).’ ” Therefore, the twenty-two thousand (22,000) people went to their home_place, and only ten thousand (10,000) were left.

9 When the sun_set, Gidyun was_told by the Lord God, “Get_ready(pl), attack(pl) their camp because I caused_ them _to_be_defeated by you(pl). 10 But if you(sg) are afraid to attack, just go_down to their camp. 13 On Gidyun and_company's arrival, there's a person that they heard telling his dream to other person. The person said, “I dreamed that there's one bread of barley that rolled_down to our(incl) camp. And our(incl) tents was hit by it and it fell and broke.”

14 And the other person answered, “No other meaning of that but rather, that is Gidyun the Israilita who_was_the child of Huwas. God cause_ the (ones) from_Midiyan and all who (are) here in our(incl) camp _to_be_defeated by him.”

15 When Gidyun heard the dream and the meaning of it, he bowed_down worshiping God. Afterwards, he returned to the camp of the Israilitas and he said, “Get_ready(pl)! 19 At the middle of the night, when the guards were newly shifting, Gidyun arrived there at the edge of the camp and the one hundred (100) persons who were with him. 23 And Gidyun summoned the Israilitas from the descendant of Naptali, Asir, and Manasis, and he caused_ them _to_chase the (ones) from_Midiyan. 24 Gidyun sent someone_to_tell to the entire mountains which were the place of the descendant of Ipraim to say, “Go_down to fight with the (ones) from_Midiyan. The defeat of (ones) from_Midiyan

81 And the people of Ipraim asked Gidyun, “Why did you(pl) do this to us(excl)? Why you(pl) didn't summoned us(excl) on your(pl) warring with the (ones) from_Midiyan?” And their complaining with Gidyun was vehement (LIT much).

21 And Gidyun was_told by Siba and Salmuna, “Hurry(sg), you_yourself(emph) the one to kill us(excl) because this isn't the work of a child.”[fn] So then Gidyun killed Siba and Salmuna and he took the decorations of the neck of their camels.

The dying of Gidyun

29 Gidyun[fn] the child of Huwas went_home to his house and he stayed_long there. 30 He had seventy (70) male children because his spouses were many. 31 He had a junior_wife who lived there in Sikim and they had a male child, whose name was Abimilik. 32 Then, Gidyun died. The leader Abimilik

91 And Abimilik the child of Gidyun[fn] went to Sikim, there at the relatives of his mother and he told them, 2 “Ask(pl) all the leaders of Sikim what they want: they want to be led by seventy (70) children of Gidyun, or just one person? Remember that I (am) a close (LIT very) relative of you(pl).”[fn] 3 Therefore the relatives of Abimilik spoke to all the leaders of Sikim. And the leaders of Sikim agreed to follow Abimilik because they were able_to_say, “He is our(incl) brother.” 4 And they gave Abimilik seventy (70) silvers from the house of their false_god Baal-Birit. And Abimilik used it to pay for the behaviorally_immoral_people and ones_who_make commotions in_order to follow him. 5 Abimilik went to Upra the home_place of his father, and his soldiers accompanied him and he also brought his seventy (70) brothers there at the top of ones stone and he killed them all there. But Hutam the youngest child of Gidyun was_able_to_run and hid. 6 And all the leaders of Sikim and Bit-Milu gathered there near the uk tree that's near the stone post there in Sikim in_order that they make Abimilik king.

The example by Hutam

7 When Hutam heard it, he went_uphill there at the peak of the mountain of Girisim and shouted, “Listen(pl) to me leaders of Sikim in_order that God will_listen to you(pl)! 8 One time, the trees went_out to choose one_who_rules them. They said to the olive tree, ‘You(sg) (are) the one to rule us(excl).’ 9 But the olive tree answered, ‘I won't turn_away_from my oil that can make people and gods famous, just to reign_over_you(pl).’ 10 And the trees said to the fig tree, ‘You(sg) (are) the one to reign_over us(excl).’ 11 But the fig tree answered, ‘I won't turn_away_from my sweet fruits, just to reign_over you(pl).’ 12 And the trees said to the grapevine, ‘You(sg) (are) the one to reign_over us(excl).’ 13 But the grapevine answered, ‘I won't turn_away_from my wine that can make people and gods happy, just to reign_over you(pl).’ 14 At the end, all the trees said to the thorn_tree, ‘Come_here(sg) and you(sg) (are) the one to rule us(incl).’ 15 And the thorn_tree answered, ‘If you(pl) like me indeed to rule with you(pl), run_for_protection to me so_that I can shade_over you(pl). But if you(pl) won't run_for_protection to me, I will_cause_ fire _to_come_out that will_burn_totally the cedar trees there in Libanun.’ ”

16 “Now, is what_ you(pl) _did to Abimilik that you(pl) made king good and correct? And that what_ you(pl) _did, is it good for Gidyun and to his family? Did you(pl) pay the good_thing that he made to you(pl)? 17 Remember(pl) that he fought_war in_order to_help you(pl). He suffered to save you(pl) from the (ones) from_Midiyan. 18 But now, you(pl) fought_against the family of my father. You(pl) killed_all his seventy (70) children there on one stone only. And you(pl) chose Abimilik the child of his female slave junior_wife to become king in Sikim because he is your(sg) relative. 19 If that's what you(pl) believed_in that you(pl) can repay the goodness of Gidyun and his family, continue(pl) that. 22 Abimilik reigned_over Israil in three years. 23 And God caused Abimilik and the leaders of Sikim to_fight_each_other. And the leaders of Sikim disobeyed Abimilik. 24 This happened in_order that Abimilik and the leaders of Sikim be_punished who helped him to kill the seventy (70) children of Gidyun. 25 And the leaders of Sikim did not like Abimilik any_more. And they commanded men on the hilltops to ambush, in_order_to rob(pl) everyone who went_by there. And that was found out by Abimelech.

26 And there's a person named Gaal that was the child of Ibid who went to Sikim and accompanied his brothers. And the leaders of Sikim didn't worry about them. 27 And the time of picking the fruits of grapevines came and the leaders of Sikim picked it. And they squeezed it and they feasted in the house of their false_god. When they were eating and drinking, they cursed Abimilik. 28 And Gaal said, “Abimilik, his father was Gidyun who was not our(incl) relative. And why are we(incl) submitting to him? It's Hamur on_the_contrary who was our(incl) father here in Sikim, and why are we(incl) making_ Abimilik _reign_over us(incl) and why are we(incl) obeying his trusted (one) Sibul? 29 If I'm your(pl) leader, we(incl) will_ indeed _defeat Abimilik. 30 Upon hearing of Sibul the leader of the city on what_ Gaal the child of Ibid _said, his anger smoked. 31 That's why he sent those someone_to_tell going_to Abimilik there to Aruma in_order to say, “Beware(sg) because Gaal the child of Ibid is here in Sikim with his brothers/cousins and they encouraged the people to disobey you(sg). 32 Therefore it's_necessary that you(sg) go with your(sg) people and make_an_ambush in the fields outside the city at night. 33 Before dawn, get_up(sg) early and attack the city. 34 Therefore in one night, Abimilik and all his people went. He separated four groups that make_an_ambush there at the outside of Sikim. 35 In the morning, Gaal the child of Ibid and he stood there at the entrance of the city. And Abimilik and his people came_out there where_ they _hid. 36 When Gaal saw them, he said to Sibul, “Look(sg)! There are people who went_down the mountains!”

37 And Gaal said again, “Look(sg) really! There are people who went_down there in the valley, and there are other group also_that come_from there to the uk tree of the sorcerer.”

38 And Sibul said to him, “Where is something_ you(sg) _boasted when you(sg) said who is indeed (sarcastic) Abimilik that we(incl) will_make (our) leader? This is the person that you(sg) mocked! Abimilik chased him and many from_Sikim lying_ wounded _in_the_ground, until there at the pathway of the entrance of the city. 41 And Abimilik returned there to Aruma. 42 On the following day, Abimilik was_informed that the (ones) from_Sikim went to their fields. 43 So then he accompanied his people and he divided (them) in three groups, and they made_ambush there in the fields. Upon seeing of Abimilik that the people of the city were going_out, he and his companions also went_out where_ they _hid and they killed the people. 44 And Abimilik and his group hurried to get_near the entrance of the city in_order to guard it, while the two groups were killing also all there in the fields. 45 And Abimilik was_fighting with the residents of the city until_the_afternoon. At the end, he won_ it _over and he killed the people. And he destroyed the city and he spread salt on the ground/soil.[fn]

46 All the leaders of Sikim were_told_early that they were attacked, therefore they hid there in strong room in the house of Baal-Birit. 47 Abimilik made_known that all the leaders of Sikim gathered there in the high house. 48 Therefore, he brought his people there on the mountains of Salmun. They took an axe and they cut some branches of a tree, they bound and carry_ (them) _on_shoulders. And he told the people who were his companions, “Hurry(pl)! follow(pl) what_ I _did.” 49 That is why they individually cut branches of a tree. 4 In the morning, they made an altar there. And they brought sacrifice(s) to burn and offerings so_that good breath/love would_return_between them and God. 5 And the Israilitas asked_each_other saying, “Which descendants didn't attend our(incl) meeting at Mispa in front of the Lord God?” (Because they had_promised that they would_kill the (one/s who) didn't go_there to the front of God.) 6 But the Israilitas were_sympathetic of their companions the descendant(s) of Binhamin. They said, “Today, Israil has lost one descendant. 7 What shall_ we(incl) _do so_that those remaining(pl) can_marry, when we(incl) promised the Lord God that we(incl) wouldn't give_in_marriage our(incl) female children to them?”

8 And they said, “Who was the descendant of Israil that wasn't included at our(incl) gathering there in front of the Lord God there at Mispa?” And they discovered that no_(one) from_Habis-Gilyad had attended the gathering. 9 They counted the people and from that, they knew that there were none from_Habis-Gilyad there. 10 Therefore, they commanded twelve thousand (12,000) soldiers that were warriors and they told (them), “Go(pl) to Habis-Gilyad and kill(pl) all the locals there, including the women and children. 11 Kill(pl) all the men including the women who had_sexual_relations already. But don't(pl) include the maidens who haven't been_sexually_active.” 12 And they found four hundred (400) marriageable_women that were locals of Habis in Gilyad and they brought the marriageable_women to their camp at Silu under_the_jurisdiction of Kanaan.

13 Then, the all descendants of Israil commanded the descendants of Binhamin there at the rocky_place of Rimun, “It's_possible now that you(pl) return_home because the conflict is finished.” 14 That's why the descendant(s) of Binhamin returned_home(pl), and they were_given by the Israilitas the marriageable_women from Habis-Gilyad. But the women weren't sufficient_to_go_around them.

15 The Israilitas were_sad for the descendant(s) of Binhamin because the Lord God removed Binhamin in the descendants of Israil. 16 And the leaders of the Israilitas said, “There's_no remaining women for the descendant(s) of Binhamin. What shall_ we(incl) _do so_that those still without spouse(s) can_marry? 17 Israil must not lose one descendant. We(excl) must do something so_that the remainder of the descendants of Binhamin will_ still _multiply. 18 But it's_ not _possible for us(incl) to cause_ our(incl) maiden children _marry them.” They were able_to_say that because they made_a_promise that they will_curse those who allow_ the descendants of Binhamin _marry_them.

19 That's why they said, “There's a feast every year there in Silu for the Lord God.” (Silu was there on the north (LIT left_side) of Bitil, which was on south (LIT right side) of Libuna, and beyond the path of Bitil going to Sikim.)

20-21 And they told the descendants of Binhamin, “Go(pl) in grapevines_field and hide(pl) there. And if the women of Silu are coming_out to dance, come_out(pl) from the grapevines_field and take(pl) those_ you(pl) _will_marry_with and bring(pl) them in your(pl) place. 22 And if there fathers or brothers protest to us(excl), we(excl) will_tell them, ‘Please cause_ them _to_marry your(pl) children because they were not given_each a unmarried_woman that we(excl) took from Habis-Gilyad. You(pl) won't be cursed because it's not you(pl) personally caused_ your(pl) children _to_marry them.’ ”

23 And the descendants of Binhamin obeyed it. While the women were dancing, each one of them chose a woman and they brought them against_their_will in_order that they marry (them). And they went_home to their living_place(s) and they built again ther towns and they lived(pl) there. 24 And the Israilitas went_home also there in their home_places and to their families.

25 [xr]At that time, Israil had no king, that's why they just did whatever_things, which they thought that (it) correct indeed.
